title: E-morphic: Scalable Equality Saturation for Structural Exploration in Logic Synthesis
problem: Technology-independent logic synthesis produces a single canonical circuit structure; missing opportunities for alternative structures that may optimize better for specific technology mappings.
motivation: Conventional logic synthesis favors specific structural biases; exploring diverse circuit representations can yield better area/delay trade-offs, but exhaustive search is computationally prohibitive.
method: E-morphic: equality saturation framework for resynthesis after technology-independent optimization; direct e-graph-circuit conversion; solution-space pruning; simulated annealing for e-graph extraction; enables parallel structural exploration before technology mapping.
key_novelty: First application of equality saturation for post-optimization structural resynthesis in logic synthesis, addressing structural bias.
contributions: Direct e-graph-circuit conversion enabling efficient equality saturation
12.54% average area saving and 7.29% delay reduction on EPFL benchmarks
limitations: Comparison limited to ABC; runtime overhead not quantified; applicability to sequential circuits not discussed.
primary_theme: Equality saturation for structural diversity in technology-independent logic synthesis
